note: STATIC interop is a MEMBER ACCESS, not a call to a function named `Class/.member`. It used to fall through to the generic-call branch and produce `f -[calls]-> String/.toUpperCase` — an edge whose target is not a symbol in the file, is not an export, and is in no `contains`: a dangling relationship, the one thing the "all extracted, resolved and emitted" contract exists to prevent. Invisible to F5 by construction, because the `calls` truth derives calls, the analyzer emitted a call, and the two agreed perfectly on an edge that pointed at nothing. TWO edges, because the static form carries one fact the instance form does not: WHICH CLASS — `(.method obj)` gets it from the receiver. THREE spellings exist and the fixture is what found the second one missing (`java.io.File./getName` was still emitting a dangling `calls -> java.io.File./getName`, a dot BEFORE the slash). The third, `String/toUpperCase`, is deliberately left as a CALL: it is identical in shape to `str/join` and `clojure.string/trim`, so promoting it would fabricate a member access for every namespace-qualified call in the corpus. The instance form keeps its single edge, which is exactly what makes the static form's second edge meaningful, and `Class.` with a trailing dot stays a constructor `instantiates`.
